conviction_note: abs_move 11 (option-implied 11.21%, kept whole because this is the first launch quarter and patient-start/enrollment numbers, which no consensus carries, are new information) times p_up 52 gives +0.44; the findings sum to +2.3 because each small positive (a director's $12m buy after quarter end, a near-zero $0.28-0.30m revenue bar that initial specialty-pharmacy stocking can clear, payer policies already posted) is sized alone, while p_up stays near 50 because all of them point against a +28 vol-point put skew and a +15% five-day run-up with no news that has already raised the bar.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $0.30m and EPS -$0.8472 (MarketBeat, 2026-11-03, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-scholar-rock-srrk-projected-to-post-quarterly-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-11-03/) and revenue $0.28m / EPS -$0.84 (GuruFocus, 2026-11-09, https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9185342/scholar-rock-srrk-prepares-to-report-q3-earnings-amid-high-pricetosales-valuation): two sources that agree. FY2026 revenue $5.3m and FY2027 $133m (Visible Alpha via S&P Global, 2026-09-23, https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/09/scholar-rock-s-isembyld-approval-sets-up-rapid-sales-ramp), so Q4 implicitly about $5m. The company has given no revenue, patient-start or expense guidance (Q2 release, https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/scholar-rock-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-recent-business-highlights). The line the stock trades on (patient starts, enrollment forms, payer coverage, Q4 commentary) has no consensus anywhere I could find.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest 22,175,999 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement (18.2% of 121.79m shares outstanding, higher as a share of float), 12.72 days to cover. It was 18.0m on 2026-08-31, 19.4m on 09-15 and 22.7m on 09-30, so shorts added about 4.7m shares after the 2026-09-11 approval and trimmed 0.5m by mid-October. The 10-30 settlement is published 2026-11-10 (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/srrk/shortinterest, read 2026-11-09). Borrow fee about 0.3% (curvedtrading snippet). Skew_25d +27.98 vol points ('downside paid'), put/call OI 0.70, total OI only 1,917, ATM spread 55% of mid, so the implied move is indicative. Tape: +15.07% over 5 days and +17.73% over 20 days, -17.8% from the 52-week high of $61.76. The stock fell from about $55-60 after approval to $39.90 on 2026-10-16 and has rallied about 24% since, with no news (AAII 2026-11-09 says no rating change in the month). That is a crowded short into a first-launch print, part of it possibly already covering.

findings.finding: Director Srinivas Akkaraju (Samsara funds) bought about 289,470 SRRK shares on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-26 (146,970 on 10-26 at an average $41.59, $6.1m; about $12m in total), 23-26 days after Q3 closed and about two weeks before the print. A board member with access to the launch's first five weeks of enrollment and shipment data was a large open-market buyer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print in the baseline came after a comparable insider purchase. Insider activity over 12 months: $12.0m bought, $19.4m sold (GuruFocus). The Q2 print (2026-08-06) moved +9.96%; the other non-regulatory prints moved within ±3.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced. The Form 4 has been public since 10-27 and the stock is up about 19% from the $41.59 purchase price. If the market had fully read the buy as a statement about launch data, the put skew would not still sit at +28 vol points and short interest would have fallen more than the 0.5m shares it did by 10-15 (the purchase came after that settlement, so the 10-30 settlement published on print day is the test).
findings.independence: Form 4 index on EDGAR (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/own-disp?action=getissuer&CIK=0001727196) and the Substack summary (https://aimandemircan.substack.com/p/scholar-rock-won-the-approval-now, 2026-10-29) record the same purchases. Both are the same fact, not independent evidence of the launch.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar is $0.28-0.30m, about 25 vials at the $11,659 WAC, for a launch that began 2026-09-11 and distributes through five specialty pharmacies (Accredo, CarePartners/Seven Bridges, CVS Specialty, Orsini, CuraScript SD). Initial channel stocking across five SPs plus 19 days of infusions could clear a bar this small several times over, though the stock trades on patient starts rather than on dollars.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the first product-revenue print in the company's history, so the name has no reaction history on this line. Rare-disease first launches are commonly judged on patient metrics; ZS reports launches that miss see year-1 estimates cut about 40% (https://www.zs.com/insights/biopharma-launches-launch-forecasting-commercial-friction).
findings.source_date: undated hub enrollment form (launch 2026-09-11); WAC $11,659 per vial per Reuters via NewsBreak 2026-09-14 https://www.newsbreak.com/reuters-555486/4885709600028-scholar-rock-says-its-first-muscle-targeted-sma-therapy-will-cost-about-310-000-annually
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus is set to almost nothing ($0.3m) and FY2026 $5.3m, so a revenue figure of $1-3m would be a large percentage beat. Whether that is in the price is unclear: if it were, the sell-side would have moved the Q3 number off a placeholder. The real bar (patient starts and enrollment forms) is unsourced, so this finding is capped small.
findings.independence: Proxy and inference: the SP network count comes from the hub form; the WAC is from Reuters. No company or counterparty number on Q3 shipments exists.

findings.finding: Payer coverage pathways were posted within about five weeks of approval. Aetna's 2026 precertification list carries Isembyld (J3490/J3590/C9399, PA via Evolent). UnitedHealthcare's Medicare Advantage Part B drug policy (file dated 2026-10-26) lists it. Wellmark's Medicare Part B PA list has it effective 2026-10-15. The add-on is being managed under prior authorization, not excluded, which is the access risk analysts flagged at approval.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the first commercial print, so there is no history on this line. Payer acceptance of an add-on was the first concern named in post-approval coverage (ts2.tech 2026-09-14), and the stock fell 4.6% on the first session after approval.
findings.source_date: 2026 list, Isembyld entry added post-2026-09-11 (search snippet); UHC policy file metadata 2026-10-26 https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/medadv-mp/medications-drugs-outpatient-partb.pdf; Wellmark PA effective 2026-10-15 https://digital-assets.wellmark.com/adobe/assets/urn:aaid:aem:c333050f-943f-421d-922a-c7cddb06a3a3/original/as/Part-B-Drugs-Prior-Authorization-List.pdf
findings.why_not_priced: Payer PDF lists are not aggregated and no preview cites them. A PA listing is normal for an orphan biologic, though, so this mainly removes an exclusion tail. If the market had read it, the downside skew would be lower.
findings.independence: Three different payers' documents. I could not read the policy criteria (the UHC PDF did not parse), so whether coverage requires stable SMN2 therapy or a functional baseline is unknown.

findings.finding: The 10-Q will disclose Q3 use of the $200m ATM (new Jefferies supplement filed 2026-08-06 at a $45.85 reference price; $257.7m net raised under the program to date; $62.8m raised in Q2). The stock traded at $52-60 for weeks after approval, so Q3/October sales are likely, along with a possible draw of the $150m Blue Owl delayed tranche available after approval. The money funds a visible launch (lesson 4), so this is close to zero, with a small dilution-headline risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print included $62.8m of ATM proceeds and moved +9.96%, so ATM use has not been punished at a print. A rallies.ai piece ties one past slide to dilution fears (undated).
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 ATM issuance is not yet public: the last share count is 121.79m on the August 10-Q cover. Part of the 4.7m-share rise in short interest after approval could be hedging of ATM supply. If the market knew the size, short interest would not be the open question it is.
findings.independence: The Substack (https://aimandemircan.substack.com/p/scholar-rock-won-the-approval-now, 2026-10-29) independently notes that no Q3 ATM data exist yet and gives the $150m delayed-draw terms. ts2.tech (2026-09-14) gives $492.1m cash at June 30, so there is no going-concern pressure.

findings.finding: Management said at approval that it plans to sell the rare pediatric disease priority review voucher it received (CFO Vikas Sinha). Recent vouchers have sold for about $150m (range $100-200m). No sale has been announced in any 8-K through 2026-11-09, so a sale disclosed with the print would add non-dilutive cash equal to about 2.5% of the $5.8-6bn market cap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This company has no history on this line. Voucher sales usually move a mid-cap by about the cash value or less.
findings.why_not_priced: Whether a sale is announced inside the window is unknown. The planned sale is public, so only the timing would be new. It is sized as a fraction because it is below the line and dilution-offsetting.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001727196) shows no 8-K since 2026-09-15, so there is no announced sale. The Goldman conference summary (https://ng.investing.com/news/transcripts/scholar-rock-at-goldman-sachs-conference-strategic-focus-on-sma-93CH-1963214) mentions about $150m comparables.

findings.finding: Positioning: short interest rose from 18.0m (08-31) to 22.7m (09-30) after approval and was 22.2m (18.2% of shares outstanding, 12.7 days to cover) at 10-15. The stock has rallied 24% off its 10-16 low of $39.90 and 15% in five sessions without news, into a print that carries the first launch metrics. Any credible patient-start number is fuel for further covering, while part of the squeeze may already have happened.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-11-14 print (+24.41%) came with heavy short interest and a regulatory update. The 2026-08-06 print moved +9.96%.
findings.why_not_priced: The 5-day run-up suggests covering has begun, which is why this is small. If the crowding were fully unwound, the 10-30 settlement (published 2026-11-10) would show it, and the put skew would be lower than +28.
findings.independence: AAII 2026-11-09 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/544584-why-scholar-rock-holding-corporation8217s-srrk-stock-is-down-581) reports +12.6% month-to-date with no rating change, consistent with flows rather than news. Benzinga's sentiment page (18.7% short float) agrees on the level.

findings.finding: The 2026-09-15 8-K corrected management: the FDA did impose a post-marketing pregnancy safety study and asked for all serious and non-serious fracture cases as 15-day alert reports (label fracture rate 9% versus 2% on placebo). The first commercial weeks can therefore surface early fracture reports that management may be asked about on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 4.6% on the first session after approval (2026-09-14), when the fracture label was one of the cited concerns.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: the correction is two months old. Only a new safety disclosure on the call would be unpriced, and nothing suggests one, so this is sized near 0 with a left tail.
findings.independence: ts2.tech (https://ts2.tech/en/scholar-rocks-first-drug-is-approved-srrk-falls-as-the-launch-test-begins/, 2026-09-14) lists fractures among investor concerns. That is the same underlying label fact.

findings.finding: Peer read-through: Biogen's Q3 2026 (released 2026-10-28) showed US Spinraza sales of $246.4m, up 60.8%, on high-dose conversion. US SMN2-treated patients are actively engaging neurologists and infusion sites, which is the setting in which an add-on IV infusion every four weeks is easiest to start. Biogen's 10-Q attributes part of the jump to stocking and a one-time transition dose.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history; this is a peer.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy. Nobody has linked Spinraza high-dose visits to Isembyld starts, and Biogen did not comment on the add-on in what I read.
findings.independence: Proxy only; no counterparty confirmation for SRRK.

outside_window.finding: EMA MAA resubmitted 2026-10-08 with the alternate fill-finish site; CHMP opinion now expected H1 2027 (was mid-2026).
UBS (2026-11-16) and Jefferies London (2026-11-17) conferences are the next management appearances after the print.

baseline_tension: Every positive here cuts against a +28 vol-point put skew and a +15% five-day run-up with no news that has already raised the bar; the crowded short (18% of shares outstanding, 12.7 days to cover) is the one reason the skew may overstate the downside, so p_up sits only just above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew): director-purchase finding trimmed +1.0 to +0.8 and payer finding +0.5 to +0.4; the stated reason the skew may be wrong is the crowded short, kept in the positioning finding.
Lesson 1 and lesson 6 (fact is not reaction; the real bar is unsourced): revenue/stocking finding cut +1.0 to +0.6, because the stock trades on patient starts, which have no consensus.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): ATM finding cut -0.5 to -0.2, because the money funds a visible launch and $492m cash rules out distress.
Lesson 2 (one-offs as fractions): voucher finding cut +0.3 to +0.2.
